title: Architecture (replan): sliced-implement-phase cleanup — context-PR topology collapse, restart hardening, dead-code purge
summary: Replan of the previously-approved issue-2777 plan against current HEAD on origin/main. The cleanup ships across two sequential slices per cq-1: slice-1 ("A+D") collapses egg/<id>/context onto egg/<id>/work, deletes the PR phase entirely (cq-4), opens the context PR up-front at the plan→implement boundary as a single hard-required idempotent gh-pr-list+create, hard-removes the redundant context_branch / context_title / context_description PRMetadata fields with a v1.1→v1.2 schema bump (cq-2), deletes orchestrator/consensus.py entirely (cq-5), subsumes the #2389 umbrella terminology rename as a structural deletion (cq-6), adds gh-pr-list idempotency to create_slice_pr (cq-8), keeps the speculative #2199 SliceScheduler hooks with noqa+docs (cq-3), bundles #2570 (silent work-branch rebase onto main) by stopping the rebase and adding an isolation invariant test, audits the ~20 BLE001 swallow-all handlers in the slice run loop individually (feedback Q2), collapses the slice-loop except-ImportError dual-path import shims to canonical orchestrator.X imports (feedback Q3), and does surgical structural extractions (_is_slice_dag_mode + slice-1-base-resolver per cq-10). Slice-2 ("C") hardens slice and phase restart: eager-persists parent_branch_at_creation under the contract lock at PENDING→IN_PROGRESS plus a merge-base fallback (cq-9), iterates per-slice consensus trackers on restart_phase, and threads slice_id through startup_reconciliation's tracker reconstruction (bundling #2409). Scope is explicitly bounded: #2792 / plan_draft_missing_on_local / _sync_worktree_with_remote / _empty_contract_hitl_* / PlanDraftMissingOnLocalError-family / _populate_contract_from_plan_safe are OUT OF SCOPE per operator directive on decision-11 + cq-7 (and #2627 is OUT per feedback Q1). NOTE: since the prior plan was approved (2026-05-27), #2792's auto-recovery has landed independently in merged PR #2797 (commit 99f8a008a8). That changes the OOS rationale from "to be handled separately" to "has already been handled independently" but does NOT expand scope here — the listed OOS primitives still must not be touched in either slice of this work.

recommended_approach.name: Two-slice sequential cleanup: A+D+PR-phase-removal → C (restart hardening)
recommended_approach.summary: Slice-1 lands the structural collapse (context-PR topology onto work, PR phase deletion, PRMetadata schema bump, umbrella terminology deletion, ConsensusEvaluator deletion, idempotency hardening for create_slice_pr, #2570 silent-rebase fix, BLE001 slice-loop audit, slice-loop ImportError shim collapse, surgical _is_slice_dag_mode + slice-1-base-resolver extraction). Slice-2 lands the restart hardening (eager-persist parent_branch_at_creation + merge-base fallback in the slice-1-base-resolver helper, per-slice consensus tracker reconstruction by threading slice_id through startup_reconciliation bundling #2409, slice-aware restart_phase that iterates per-slice trackers). Sequential because slice-2's restart hardening reasons about the post-collapse topology — the moment slice-1 ships, slice-2 no longer has to consider the separate egg/<id>/context branch in its reconciliation logic and reuses the slice-1-base-resolver helper that slice-1 creates.
why_recommended: Issue explicitly favours deletion; cq-1 chose the two-slice sequential shape with A+D bundled because most dead-code (D) services the context-PR scaffold (A); splitting them creates merge conflicts inside _run_implement_phase_slices and the ~600-line context-PR scaffold.

Three prior iterations (#2593, #2744, #2769) of symptom-fix-only on the context-PR class did not converge. The cleanup makes the design idempotent-by-construction: one gh-pr-list + one gh-pr-create at the plan→implement boundary, hard-required, replaces the soft-fail wrapper called from five sites.

The PR phase deletion (cq-4) is structurally cleaner than the original "backstop" framing — once the up-front open is atomic and hard-required, there is no silent-failure path to back-stop, so the PR phase becomes dead weight. This also obviates the _should_skip_pr_phase_auto_pr branch that hid the slice-DAG case from the existing backstop.

Bundling #2570 into slice-1 is necessary, not optional: the new context-PR model is head=egg/<id>/work base=main, which means a silently-rebased work branch directly threatens the new design's isolation invariant. Diagnosing and stopping the rebase has to land alongside the topology change.

Slice-2 separated from slice-1 because the restart-hardening surface is bounded and self-contained (per-slice tracker reconstruction + parent_branch_at_creation timing) and benefits from landing after slice-1 simplifies the topology it has to reconcile.

technical_decisions.rationale: The 'backstop' framing only existed because the original up-front open was a multi-step non-atomic operation that could silently fail (return None paths × ~21). Once the open is one gh-pr-list + maybe one gh-pr-create — hard-required, no soft-fail — there is no silent-failure path to back-stop, so the PR phase is dead weight. Operator-directed in cq-4.
technical_decisions.alternatives_rejected: Backstop variants in cq-4's original three options (backstop opens only context PR / also re-verifies slice PRs / also reposts program-level body). All rejected because they keep the PR phase alive with non-trivial logic; operator chose deletion.
